name: Die Cut Logo Stickers
seoTitle: Die Cut Logo Stickers Cut to Your Brand Mark Outline
seoDescription: Die cut logo stickers printed in your brand colors and cut to the outline of the mark, for laptops, bottles, packaging and equipment. Free proof.
tagline: Your brand mark printed in Pantone-matched color and cut to its own outline.
quickAnswer: Die cut logo stickers are a brand mark printed on white, clear or holographic vinyl and cut to the outline of the logo itself, with no square or circle around it. They suit businesses that want the logo on laptops, bottles, packaging, hard hats and equipment. Sizes run from 0.5 inches to 24 by 36 inches, pricing starts from $0.30 per sticker with a 100 piece minimum, and production takes 5 to 7 business days after proof approval.
highlights: Material: white, clear or holographic vinyl
Finish: gloss, matte or spot UV

sections.h2: A logo cut to its own outline
sections.html:
Most logo stickers are a logo inside a shape: a circle, a rounded square, a rectangle with a border. That works when the logo is a badge. It fails when the mark has a silhouette of its own, a bird, a mountain, a letterform with a tail, because the box around it is what people see first. A die cut logo sticker removes the box. The cut follows the outline of the mark with a small margin, through the vinyl and the backing, so the sticker is the logo and nothing else.

The nearest sibling is our custom promotional stickers page. Promotional stickers carry a campaign: a slogan, a QR code, a date, a giveaway design that changes each season, often in a standard shape to keep the cost down. Logo stickers carry the mark only, in the brand color, and get reordered unchanged for years. When the sticker needs to say more than the logo, the custom promotional sticker page is the better fit.

sections.h2: Logo shapes that cut well and ones that fight the blade
sections.html:
The cutting blade follows the outline we draw around the mark. Some logos make that easy; some need a little help before they will survive peeling.

  • Badges, circles and shields cut cleanly at any size down to 0.75 inches
  • Mascots and icons with one solid silhouette cut well; add a border of 0.0625 inches to hide any registration shift
  • Wordmarks with separate letters need a shape behind them, or each letter becomes its own sticker
  • Thin tails, antennae and serifs under 0.1 inches wide tear when the backing is peeled, so we fatten them or bridge them
  • Counters inside letters such as A, B and O stay printed, not cut out, unless the sticker is over 4 inches
  • Very fine stroke logos work better as a printed outline on a simple cut shape than as a cut of every stroke

We check all of this on the proof and suggest a fix where needed, which is usually a thin keyline in a brand color or a white halo. Finishes that change how the logo reads, such as spot UV on the mark only or a holographic base, are listed under our stickers by feature category.

sections.h2: Where businesses put their logo stickers
sections.html:
Laptops and water bottles are the obvious homes, and a 2.5 to 3 inch logo is the size that fits both. The less obvious placements are often the ones that earn their keep: a 1 inch logo sealing a shipping box so the first thing a customer touches is the brand; a 2 inch mark on the back of a hard hat or a tool case on a job site; a 4 inch logo on the door of a trailer or on equipment that gets rented out; a 1.5 inch mark on a tasting glass at an event.

Outdoor placements need the laminated version. Sun and rain do not harm the vinyl, but they dull unprotected ink over a couple of years, and a laminate keeps the brand color true for longer. For an event or a night venue, the same logo prints on a glow film that charges under room light and glows for hours; our glow in the dark sticker page shows how that film handles color.

sections.h2: Ordering a die cut logo sticker in five steps
sections.html:
1. Send the logo as a vector file (AI, EPS, SVG or PDF) with the Pantone references noted. A 300 dpi PNG with a transparent background is the fallback.
  2. Give the width in inches. Height follows the logo proportion, and we quote by the larger dimension.
  3. Choose the material: white matte, white gloss, clear or holographic vinyl, with or without laminate.
  4. Approve the free digital proof, which shows the cut line in magenta and the color match.
  5. Production takes 5 to 7 business days after approval, and FedEx delivers free within the United States, 8 to 10 business days in total.

sections.h2: Color accuracy for a brand mark
sections.html:
A logo sticker in the wrong red is worse than no sticker at all. Send the Pantone number and we match it in CMYK on the press, then show the result on the proof. Matte and gloss shift the perceived color slightly, matte a little softer, gloss a little deeper, so if you are ordering both, approve both proofs. Pure brand colors outside the CMYK range, such as some oranges and bright blues, get the closest achievable match and we tell you on the proof when that is the case.

Reorders use the saved artwork and press settings, so a batch ordered next year matches the one on your laptop today. The minimum is 100 per design, sizes of the same logo count together, and pricing starts from $0.30 per sticker. Every other format we print, from sheets to large decals, runs on the same color management described on our main custom sticker page, so a logo ordered as a sticker and later as a window decal still matches.

faqs.q: How do you cut a die cut logo sticker with separate letters?
faqs.a: We draw a single shape behind the letters, usually a rounded rectangle or a smooth outline that hugs the whole word, and cut that. The letters stay printed on it. Cutting each letter separately would give you a bag of tiny stickers that cannot be aligned by hand, so we flag it on the proof and suggest the backing shape.

faqs.q: Can my die cut logo sticker match our Pantone brand color?
faqs.a: Yes. Send the Pantone number and we match it in CMYK, then show the result on the free proof before printing. Most brand colors land within a close visual match. A few very bright oranges, greens and blues sit outside the CMYK range; in those cases we show the nearest achievable color and say so.

faqs.q: What size should a die cut logo sticker be for a laptop?
faqs.a: Between 2.5 and 3.5 inches on the long side. That fits the lid of a 13 to 16 inch laptop without crowding the manufacturer's own logo, and it stays readable across a desk. For water bottles use 2 to 2.5 inches so the logo does not wrap too far around the curve.

faqs.q: Do you add a border to die cut logo stickers?
faqs.a: Only if you want one. A border of about 0.0625 inches in white or a brand color hides any tiny shift between print and cut and gives a crisp edge. Without a border we cut tight to the artwork with a 0.125 inch bleed behind it. Badges and circles usually go borderless; mascots and illustrations usually get the border.

faqs.q: Can a die cut logo sticker be printed on clear or holographic vinyl?
faqs.a: Yes, both. Clear vinyl with a white ink layer makes the logo look painted onto glass or a bottle. Holographic vinyl puts a rainbow shift under the mark, which works for icons and monograms and less well for logos with a lot of small text. White vinyl in matte or gloss remains the default for color accuracy.

faqs.q: Are die cut logo stickers good for hard hats and tool cases?
faqs.a: Yes, in the laminated version. The laminate takes the scuffs from being thrown in a truck and the sun on a job site, and the permanent adhesive holds on the smooth shell of a hard hat. Keep the sticker under 2.5 inches on a hat so it sits on the flat area and away from vents and the brim.

faqs.q: How small can a die cut logo sticker go?
faqs.a: Down to about 0.75 inches for a simple badge or icon, and 0.5 inches for a solid shape with no detail. Below that, text is unreadable and the backing is hard to peel. For box seals and tasting glasses, 1 to 1.5 inches is the practical range that still shows the mark clearly.

faqs.q: Can I get die cut logo stickers that glow in the dark?
faqs.a: Yes. The logo prints on a glow-in-the-dark vinyl that charges under room light or daylight and glows green for several hours in the dark. The film has a pale green tint by day, so brand colors read a little softer; dark logos on the glow film give the strongest effect at night.

faqs.q: What file should I send for a die cut vinyl logo?
faqs.a: A vector file, AI, EPS, SVG or a PDF exported from a vector program, with fonts converted to outlines and Pantone references noted. Vector gives us an exact cut path. If all you have is a raster logo, send a 300 dpi PNG with a transparent background and our designers will trace the outline before the proof.

faqs.q: Do die cut logo stickers hold up outdoors on equipment?
faqs.a: The laminated version does, typically for three to five years on a smooth painted or metal surface. The laminate keeps UV and abrasion off the ink. Unlaminated stickers are fine for laptops, bottles and packaging, but an outdoor generator or a trailer door needs the laminate.

faqs.q: How many die cut logo stickers come in the smallest order?
faqs.a: 100 stickers per design, and you can split that across sizes of the same logo, for example 60 at 3 inches and 40 at 1.5 inches. Pricing starts from $0.30 per sticker and depends on size, material and quantity, so a quote with your dimensions gives the exact number.

faqs.q: Can I order the same logo in several sizes at once?
faqs.a: Yes. Sizes of the same artwork share the proof and count together toward the 100 piece minimum, so a laptop size, a bottle size and a box seal size can run as one order. Each size is priced by its own dimensions, and they ship together, sorted by size, in one box.
